correctness.rationale: Direct Mellin-beta calculation establishes the shift multiplier and coefficient. The exact power norm is a strictly convex unimodal product; its log has quadratic term -pi|a| n^2/4 and a uniformly bounded remainder after the linear correction. Gaussian summation gives the resolvent upper bound. For each optimized power, a normalized short-interval Mellin input makes all Neumann terms orthogonal, giving a phase-uniform matching lower bound. Spectral-range and noncompactness statements follow from multiplication on nonatomic L2. The source and finite numerical checks were inspected; finite checks are not used as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: A 2026 existence construction of noncompact quasinilpotent Hankel operators poses a natural quantitative pseudospectral question. The exact 1/(pi|a|) resolvent coefficient measures how the noncompact operator can have an essential singularity despite spectrum {0}; it complements Gaussian-decaying yet noncompact power norms. The lower bound is sharp and prevents a superficial upper-only estimate. The problem is a motivated full-parameter canonical model rather than a tiny unmotivated example.
